label: Postural collapse
summary: Postural collapse is what happens physically when you get tired during online meetings: you sink in on yourself, your head droops toward the screen, you blink less, and your awareness of your surroundings narrows. It is both a symptom of online fatigue and something that feeds back into making that fatigue worse. Maaike treats it as a bodily phenomenon sitting alongside the more commonly discussed communicative or cultural causes of Zoom exhaustion.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses postural collapse as the entry point for practical, body-based advice about surviving online meetings. Rather than focusing only on communication friction or organisational culture, she points out that the body itself signals and amplifies exhaustion. Her tips work the other direction: by noticing your sit bones, grounding your feet, and imagining an upward flow through the spine, you can interrupt the collapse before it becomes total. She is careful to say this is about gentle awareness rather than forced tension, and frames it as something you can check in on periodically during a meeting.
open_questions: How quickly does postural collapse set in, and are some people or meeting formats more vulnerable to it than others?
Maaike gestures at a bidirectional relationship between posture and fatigue, but does not spell out the mechanism — is one direction stronger than the other?
